title: 🔅🔅TEHRAN, NOVEMBER 4 – Mohammad Javad Larijani, senior expert on international affairs and head of the Institute for Research in Fundamental Sciences, said the Iranian people have a serious demand for a change in the country's nuclear doctrine in an interview with Fars News Agency.
text:
🔅🔅TEHRAN, NOVEMBER 4 – Mohammad Javad Larijani, senior expert on international affairs and head of the Institute for Research in Fundamental Sciences, said the Iranian people have a serious demand for a change in the country's nuclear doctrine in an interview with Fars News Agency."

""
"========="

"SOT1, Mohammad Javad Larijani, a senior expert on international affairs (Farsi) (00:00 - 00:41): "We are a member of the NPT and, in accordance with our commitments, have not pursued nuclear weapons and will not do so as long as we remain a member. The fatwa issued by our martyred Imam [Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei] also prohibited weapons of mass destruction, including chemical and nuclear weapons. However, our membership in the NPT has brought us no benefits, only disadvantages. In my view, Parliament should quickly withdraw from its practical commitments under the NPT. Then let them argue with us. If they insist that we remain a member of the NPT, why should we?""

"SOT2, Mohammad Javad Larijani, a senior expert on international affairs (Farsi) (00:42 - 01:37): "How much would possessing nuclear weapons actually contribute to deterrence within our defense doctrine? This is a very important issue, and people have a serious demand on this matter as well. God willing, officials will pay attention to it. We must consider the Supreme Leader's final position, as this is ultimately a matter for him to decide. However, nuclear knowledge and technology extend far beyond simply building a bomb; building a bomb is easy compared with acquiring the knowledge behind it. The enemy wants us to lose that knowledge. My objection is also to entering negotiations in a way that focuses on our scientific and technological capabilities. As for discussing whether we should remain in or withdraw from the NPT, that is a separate matter.
